_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'History Syllabus, Ordinary Level Secondary Education, Form 1-4' (2024) for topic/sub-topic/specific-competence/expected-standard text; 'History Teaching Module, Form 1 - Term 1' (CDC, 2025) confirms Term 1 covers exactly Topics 1.1-1.4. Terms 2-3 are intentionally omitted until their own Teaching Module documents are sourced and confirmed.

subject.name: History
subject.description: Ordinary Level Secondary History syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre, 2024).

grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source syllabus itself uses "Form 1-4" for Ordinary Level Secondary under the 2023 CBC, not "Grade".

topics.name: 1.1 Introduction to History
topics.description: Reasons for learning history, local history, types/branches of history, sources of history, and using digital resources to learn about the past.

sub_topics.name: 1.1.1 Reasons for Learning History
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: relevance of past events communicated correctly.

learning_objectives.description: Explaining the meaning of History (past events)
Describing past events in the family (funerals, weddings, outings)
Describing the importance of past events (past experience can provide present or future solutions, become better citizens, develop critical thinking)
Showing the importance of history in different fields and topics (Medicine, Music, Law)

sub_topics.name: 1.1.2 Local History
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: local history interpreted accordingly.

learning_objectives.description: Discussing the history of your township/village
Analysing the developments that have taken place in your township/village in the recent past
Examining the importance of local history

sub_topics.name: 1.1.3 Types or Branches of History
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: types or branches of history classified correctly.

competencies.description: Classify types or branches of history

learning_objectives.description: Identifying types/branches of history study (Chronological: Ancient, Medieval, Modern; Thematic: Political, Social, Economic; Geographical: World History, African History; Music history, Sports history)
Classifying branches of history

sub_topics.name: 1.1.4 Sources of History
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: credibility of sources of historical information assessed appropriately.

competencies.description: Assess credibility of sources of historical information

learning_objectives.description: Discussing methods of gathering information about the past (Oral tradition, Written records, Anthropology, Archaeology, Linguistics, Genetics)
Analysing the reliability of methods of gathering information about the past
Utilising reliable methods to write history

sub_topics.name: 1.1.5 Learning About the Past Using Digital Resources
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: digital resources applied in learning about the past correctly.

competencies.description: Apply digital resources in learning about the past

learning_objectives.description: Identifying digital resources (phone, computer)
Using digital resources to find out new information about the past

topics.name: 1.2 Measuring Time in History
topics.description: Historical durations and chronology, constructing timelines, and using BC/BCE and AD/CE.

sub_topics.name: 1.2.1 Periods of Time
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: patterns of historical durations explored accordingly.

learning_objectives.description: Mentioning historical durations (year, decade, generation, century, millennium)
Calculating number of years in a given period
Converting a year into a century

sub_topics.name: 1.2.2 Importance of Chronology in History
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: series of related events arranged in chronological order correctly.

competencies.description: Arrange series of related events in chronological order

learning_objectives.description: Explaining the meaning of chronology
Arranging identified prominent events in our family, community, country and international chronologically

sub_topics.name: 1.2.3 Constructing a Timeline
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: chronology in writing timeline applied correctly.

competencies.description: Apply chronology in writing time line

learning_objectives.description: Discussing types of time lines (progressive, regressive, pictorial)
Constructing a personal timeline under specified guidelines
Constructing events timeline under specified guidelines
Describing the importance of a timeline

sub_topics.name: 1.2.4 The Use of Abbreviations to Denote Historical Periods
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: use of abbreviations (BC/BCE and AD/CE) to denote historical periods demonstrated correctly.

competencies.description: Use abbreviations (BC/BCE and AD/CE) to denote historical periods

learning_objectives.description: Explaining the meaning of abbreviations BC or BCE and AD or CE
Counting years in BC and AD
Demonstrating the use of BC/BCE and AD/CE to a given date
Calculating the number of years between two given periods of time

topics.name: 1.3 The Origins of Man (Human Being)
topics.description: Religious and scientific views on the origins of man.

sub_topics.name: 1.3.1 Views on the Origins of Man
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: religion and scientific views on the origins of man analysed accordingly.

competencies.description: Analyse religious and scientific views on the origins of man

learning_objectives.description: Describing creation of man according to religion (Christianity and Islam)
Explaining the beginning of life on earth according to scientists (Charles Darwin's theory)
Contrasting religious and scientific views on the origins of man

topics.name: 1.4 Stone Age
topics.description: The way of life in the Stone Age and Stone Age sites in Zambia.

sub_topics.name: 1.4.1 The Way of Life in Stone Age
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: lessons from Stone Age way of life drawn appropriately.

competencies.description: Draw lessons from Stone Age way of life

learning_objectives.description: Classifying Stone Age (Paleolithic/Early, Mesolithic/Middle, Neolithic/Late Stone Age)
Identifying creatures that existed in the three Stone Ages (Early: Homo-Habilis; Middle: Broken Hillman; Late: Bushmen/San)
Describing social, political, economic aspects of the Stone Age
Analysing the use of various Stone Age tools (hunting, cutting, digging)
Contrasting Stone Age way of life with modern way of life

sub_topics.name: 1.4.2 Stone Age Sites in Zambia
sub_topics.description: Expected standard: importance of Stone Age sites in Zambia assessed appropriately.

competencies.description: Assess importance of Stone Age sites in Zambia

learning_objectives.description: Locating Stone Age sites on the map of Zambia (Mwela Rocks, Nachikufu Caves, Gwisho Hot Springs)
Analysing the importance of Stone Age sites (tourism, cultural heritage)
